stories.body: Russian bombs struck a school used as a shelter and humanitarian aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha, in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 26 people, Ukrainian officials said. The dead included two rescue workers and four police officers. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the attack came as residents arrived for aid and was followed by a second strike on the shelter. It came after a temporary ceasefire that allowed evacuations from Russian-occupied Oleshky. US-led talks between Russia and Ukraine are expected to resume in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11.
stories.headline: Russian strike on Ukrainian aid centre kills at least 26

stories.body: The US carried out limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island on Monday, according to US media reports cited by Reuters and the Associated Press. The strikes reportedly targeted surface-to-air missiles being used against US assets. Iranian state media reported explosions but did not identify their cause, and US Central Command did not immediately comment. The reports came as Vice President JD Vance expressed optimism about indirect talks with Tehran to end the conflict; Iran continues to restrict shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.headline: US reportedly strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island as talks continue

stories.body: About 2,800 troops from European countries will take part in an exercise in Poland from November 9 to 22 to test how a multinational force could deploy to Ukraine after a peace deal. Led by Britain and France, the exercise will rehearse moving, protecting and supplying the force. Western officials say any eventual deployment would help reassure Ukraine and rebuild its armed forces, rather than conduct offensive operations or monitor a ceasefire. Russia has opposed the presence of foreign troops in Ukraine.
stories.headline: European troops to rehearse possible Ukraine deployment

stories.body: Supermarkets in several European countries reported refrigeration failures on Monday, with some confirming cyberattacks after temperatures in fridges and freezers rose as high as 50°C. Retailers in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden were among those affected, and some stores discarded food. The incidents followed an attack on hundreds of French supermarkets last month that caused fires and extensive food losses. The EU’s food and agriculture commissioner called the attacks a deliberate attempt to disrupt the food supply chain.
stories.headline: Cyberattack disrupts supermarket refrigeration across Europe

stories.body: The Ebola outbreak centred in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed 5,376 people across three countries, according to Africa CDC data released Monday. Of those deaths, 5,372 were in DR Congo and two each were in Kenya and Uganda. The Bundibugyo strain has infected about 10,444 people across the three countries. There are no approved vaccines or treatments specifically for that strain, though trials have begun using the Ervebo vaccine, which is effective against the Zaire strain.
stories.headline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has killed more than 5,300 people

stories.body: Australia’s High Court began hearing challenges by Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project to the country’s ban on social media accounts for children under 16. Reddit argues that the law restricts young people’s ability to participate in political communication and was rushed through parliament. The government says the measure protects children from online harms. Since the ban took effect last December, platforms have suspended or deactivated more than five million accounts they believe belong to under-16s.
stories.headline: Australia’s high court hears challenge to social media ban for under-16s

stories.body: Americans are voting in midterm elections that could shift control of one or both chambers of Congress from Republicans to Democrats. Candidates made their final appeals on Monday, with the outcome set to determine how much power Democrats have to check President Donald Trump during the remainder of his term.
stories.headline: Americans vote in midterms with control of Congress at stake

stories.body: Republican candidates, lawmakers and campaign officials are privately blaming President Donald Trump for putting the party at risk in the midterms, Politico reports. People interviewed pointed to the Iran war’s effect on fuel and fertilizer prices, tariffs and immigration enforcement as liabilities in competitive races. Few have criticized Trump publicly, and the White House and Republican National Committee defended his role in the campaign. The scale of any losses could shape debate over the party’s direction toward 2028.
stories.headline: Republicans privately blame Trump as they brace for midterm losses

stories.body: Texas Republicans’ unusual mid-decade redistricting is being tested at the polls after the party redrew congressional boundaries at President Donald Trump’s urging. In Houston, the new map moved a predominantly Black community from the ninth district into the Black-majority 18th, where incumbent Christian Menefee defeated fellow Democrat Al Green in a primary. The redrawn ninth district now favours Republicans. Critics say the map concentrates Black voters in fewer districts and weakens their representation.
stories.headline: Midterms test Republican redistricting in Texas

stories.body: Transport Minister Óscar Puente is due to present measures to improve rail safety and help victims of the Urda high-speed train crash to the cabinet on Tuesday. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said the government would approve specific aid and advance compensation for those affected. The collision in Toledo province killed at least 69 people and was Spain’s second fatal high-speed rail accident in nine months, undermining public confidence in the network.
stories.headline: Spain prepares rail safety measures and aid for Urda victims

stories.body: The train drivers’ union SEMAF has called strikes for November 10 and 12 as railway unions consider wider action to demand stronger safety measures after the Urda crash. The walkouts fall on either side of a planned general strike. Minimum service requirements will apply, but disruption to train services is expected across the three days.
stories.headline: Train drivers plan strikes on November 10 and 12

stories.body: The Guardia Civil has questioned about 20 people in its investigation into the Urda train crash, most of them railway workers who were at Adif’s Madrid-Atocha control centre when a Renfe train struck an Iryo train. One Adif operator, who was called in as a person under investigation and accompanied by a lawyer, exercised his right not to answer questions. According to released audio, he had authorized the first train to proceed normally while the other was still stopped on the track.
stories.headline: Guardia Civil questions about 20 people in Urda investigation

stories.body: Spanish parties are adjusting their campaigns for the November 29 general election after the Urda rail disaster. Frente Amplio and Podemos are preparing to campaign on housing and basic rights while warning of a possible PP–Vox government. PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has emphasized his party’s management experience and said Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez should answer to Congress over the crash; he also said he would have dismissed Transport Minister Óscar Puente.
stories.headline: Urda crash reshapes Spain’s election campaign

stories.body: Barcelona plans to connect the Trambaix and Trambesòs lines along the full length of Avinguda Diagonal in the first quarter of 2031. The city is tendering the remaining 2.8-kilometre section between Verdaguer and Francesc Macià, with construction expected to begin next summer and finish in late 2030 before testing. The €120 million project includes three new stops, street improvements and expanded stormwater drainage. The city expects the completed line to carry 75 million passengers a year.
stories.headline: Barcelona expects Diagonal tram connection to open in early 2031

stories.body: Catalan president Salvador Illa says he prefers to keep the Barcelona–Madrid high-speed rail line operating during planned renovations, provided safety can be maintained. Transport Minister Óscar Puente had raised the possibility of a temporary closure after the Urda crash. The line’s renovation is expected to begin around the end of this year or early in 2027. Transport expert Joan Carles Salmerón called a full closure unworkable, saying there is no adequate alternative for its tens of thousands of daily passengers.
stories.headline: Illa favours keeping Barcelona–Madrid high-speed line open during works

stories.body: Eduard Rivas has resigned as chief of staff to Catalan president Salvador Illa amid a judicial investigation into public contracts from his time as mayor of Esparreguera. The investigation concerns contracts involving a labour inclusion foundation on whose board Rivas served. He says he acted lawfully and stepped down to avoid casting doubt on the government. Xavier Amor, until now the Catalan government’s secretary for local government and relations with Aran, is expected to replace him.
stories.headline: Catalan president’s chief of staff resigns amid investigation

stories.body: Police have arrested two girls aged 14 and 17 over their alleged role in promoting the October 24 disturbances and looting in Barcelona through Blocus messaging channels. Police say they administered groups used to coordinate the actions, which were promoted through a TikTok post linking to a WhatsApp channel. Separately, a judge ordered a 21-year-old held without bail in connection with the investigation. Barcelona’s juvenile courts have ordered five minors held in closed facilities following the disturbances.
stories.headline: Two teenagers arrested over alleged promotion of Barcelona looting

stories.body: Barcelona has introduced nine staffed mobile recycling points in the Gòtic and Sant Pere, Santa Caterina i la Ribera neighbourhoods to make sorting waste easier and reduce rubbish bags left on streets. The points operate mornings and afternoons from Monday to Saturday except holidays, with staff advising residents on sorting. The city says a pilot reduced abandoned bags by 30% to 42%. Each Ciutat Vella neighbourhood also now has one designated evening per week for putting out unwanted furniture and bulky items.
stories.headline: Ciutat Vella introduces mobile recycling points
